text:
بلکه ده لازمه‌ء تجارون برجل بزرگوار • و فرقه اخیاردن بر مرد عالی مقدار •
بو معدن مارب و مطالب صورته کتاب العجایب والغرایب کوندرب لسرع اپ فضل
و فضلیت • هر عالمی که قبل اینکه عنان تمت دو ندرب بلکه بیر ده کو کره مرزکم آ
او لاعالم محیطی آکه شامل • هر بی بوامره بناء بنده که‌نه‌سند فرمان ایلدی • بو کتابه شرح
و بیان ایله دی مثنوی پس شروع اتدم کتابک ترحمه • زاید اولانان لچیدن طرحنه •
داخل نمایدم فواید غیرن • تاکه نظم ایده انه [...] بلکل که ظاهر آسمان وزینه
عین بهایم دخر کورر • آما بل نظر قتده اول نظرمعبر [...] بلکه فکر صریح ونظر صحیح
اولدر که بوترکب • یانه واحوال معلوم اولوب • و برو [...] اسرار آنیه مفهوم اولا •
حکمت صانع مطلق نظام راولوب • عاقل ولان نفع شکراولا • انوکچون رسول الله
علیه الصلوة والسلام اتنا الاشیا کاهی دبودعا ایراریدی و مرته ذکه وحق بقله
حضرت نکه صنوعاتده فکر زیاد اولایقین وایمان وتحقیق واذعان زیاده اونور
ذ نوکچون رسوالن الله صلی الله علیه وسلم بوررتفکروا فی خلق الله وتعقل معقل
اولنه [...] اتمام ایدرکه علومن ریاضاتدن خیر داراولا وآهلا قنه حسنه ایلمش
و تهذیب نفس ایلمشی ولاائدن صکره آننک بصیره کوزی احبلور لبر حیر نیه نظر ایله
اندن عجیب اسنه لرکوبرراکر آندن بعضنه برعروض ایلدیکه اول معنی دانپری
اولمشه منکراولوروتو عبلدون دخضر وموسی علیهما السلام قصه‌ای خویل
وعالا قرآن نبید ده حکایتایدبدر وقتوندن دحکایت موسی علیه السلام •
translation: Rather it is incumbent upon the great merchant, and among the select men of high standing. This treasury of wonders and subjects — the book of marvels and rarities (Kitāb al-ʿAjāʾib wa'l-Gharāʾib) — having been presented and its excellence and merit made known to every scholar before, and encompassing all knowledge in its compass — by command of that servant a commentary and explanation was made of this book. I then began the translation (tercüme) of this book in verse (mathnawī), setting aside whatever was superfluous. I did not include extraneous benefits, so that the arrangement might appear, manifesting like the adornment of the heavens — for even an animal sees with its eyes, but true reflection and sound observation is that which perceives the composition: that the states and conditions become known, and the secrets within comprehended, and the wisdom of the Absolute Creator becomes apparent in its order, so that the rational person may give thanks. For this reason, the Messenger of God — upon whom be blessings and peace — used to pray and invoke [God] constantly, and by right of contemplation of the works of creation, faith, conviction and certainty increase, and light grows. For this reason the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: 'Reflect upon the creation of God' (tafakkarū fī khalq Allāh) — and let the rational person understand. Let one complete the sciences of the mathematical disciplines and be among the people of good deeds, having refined one's soul. Thereafter the eye of insight opens and one beholds wonders. If one of those wonders is presented — [it is said that] the one who has come to know that meaning will deny it and call it impossible. Regarding Khiḍr and Moses — upon them both be peace — there is a lengthy and elevated story, a narrative found in the Qurʾān, and from that time the story of Moses — upon him be peace.
page_note: text page: introduction/preface discussing the purpose and method of the Ottoman Turkish verse translation of the Aja'ib al-makhluqat

text:
وحى آلاى نازل اولدى كه فلان يرده برحيثه واردراندن آهرست اولو بطاع اوزر
وارب ممانه مشغول اولاسن موسى عليه السلام اويله ايلدى آتفا ق برآتلوكسه
كلوب اول چشمه دن صواجبوب وآنذه كيسه ايله اقيسن فراموش ايدوب آندن صو
برجوبان كلوبكيسه يه ايذه بولوب آلوب كيدوب وآندن صوكره برير بركلور كه
ارقاسنده برقوجاق اودون واركوندوده آثارفقط طامراو دون بنده آنده
قوبصودن اجوب راحت اولق اچون برلظه اوتورب آتلوا قيسن اكوب
استعمال ايله كلوب ايفه كيسه نين بولمبوب آل بردن سؤال ايدوب اول بير
سنكورهدم والمدم ديوب آولآتلوغضبه كلوب بيرى اورب بلاك ايليوب
موسى عليه السلام بواحوالى مشاهده ايدوب حناب حقه مناجات ايليوب كه
يارب بونجه عدل در حضرت حق وحى كونزدى كه اول بيرسابقا اول آتلو نكر بابان
قتل ايدوب فصاص اولمنوب قالمش ايدى وآوآل آتلوكسه دجو انك بابالنك
اول كيسه ده اولان مقدار ماراولوب قالمش ايدى آتلو يراوندوب حيانه
بولوروب مريرنكه حقى دنياده صاحبه حقه ايصال ايتدم وانا الحكم بالعد
بوندن معلوم اولدى كه اسراراآرآهيزمركسيظاهرا اولمز آتا مؤلف كتاب بمع وبهر
ونظر ايقى يا بعض چكم عجيبه وخواص غريبه جاصل انمش ايدى آتلدى كتاب بلمق قرو نا
طونق ديلدى كه رسول الله عليه الضاء والسلام بيورمش در قيدوا العلم بالكاتبة
بسعلم بازلتق ايله ثابت اولوروغر [...] ه دحى فايده اولوروكوتابده بعض لسند لر
translation: A divine revelation descended [saying]: 'Go to such-and-such a place, in such a manner, and attend to obedience therein.' Moses (peace be upon him) did accordingly. A [man] came and drank from that spring, and then forgot his purse and went away. A shepherd came, found the purse, took it and left. Then afterward there came a man who had on his back a bundle of firewood, who sat down for a moment to rest and take a breath, to make use [of the spring]. He came and, not finding the purse, asked about it. [The shepherd] said to him: 'None of your business,' and in anger struck and killed him. Moses (peace be upon him) witnessed all these events and supplicated to the Divine Presence, [saying]: 'O Lord, where is justice in all this?' The Divine Presence revealed: 'O Moses, that [first man who took the purse] had previously slain that [man's] father and escaped retaliation (qisas). The amount of money that was in that purse was equivalent to what [the shepherd] owed [the murdered man's] father. The killer was thus made to pay the blood-price, and the rightful one was given his due in this world. And I am the Judge in justice (wa ana al-hukm bi-l-'adl).' From this it is understood that the secrets of [Divine] wisdom are not always apparent to everyone. The author of this book, having collected wonders and rarities and peculiar properties that had been obtained [from various sources], compiled the book so that it might be read and known. The Messenger of God (may God's blessings and peace be upon him) said: 'Preserve knowledge by writing it down (Qayyadū al-'ilm bi-l-kitāba).' Knowledge established through writing is beneficial and [remains as] lasting benefit, and some of the copyists of this book [...]
page_note: text page: narrative on divine justice (Moses anecdote) and preface on the purpose of the book

text:
واردر که ذهن کودن کا تشخیل ولیوب انکار ایدر آما ذهن ذکی بلردن برنه منکر اولمز زیرا
حق تعالی قدرت قوی در مکان اولاز ایجاد ایده بیلور وآول نسنه لر که کوتاریده مذکور
aolور یا عجایب صنع باری تعالی در که بعض محسوس اولوب وبعضی دلیل عقلی ایله معلوم
aolوب وتعجب زاویدن سموع اولب یا بلش ریا خواص غریبه در که بر خبریه ایله معلوم اتمثلاً
بر کشی بر خبریه ایده وبلکه عمر اکا وفات امرز واگر حالیا بر خبریه ایله بعضنه مخلف
واقع اولسا انکار اتمک اولمه لا معنی لترک الامور کلها لاجل المثلث فی بعضها
زیرا کاه اولور تخلف بر شرط بولنمغ عندان اولور یا بر مانع اولد و عندان اولور کرگذر که
از مقناطیس ایله مور حالنه قیاس ایده من که اگر مساقات ققه سی مناطیه یکرشه
خاصیت مقناطیس باطل اولور وچون سر که ایله وسطه لر خاصیتنی کر وعودت قبلور
آمدی اکر بر مقناطیسی کور سنگ ده مورقابز ده به سن که مقناطس ومور قابز تکله
تفیثلیروب کور مک کرک نا معلوم اولا که مانع نذر وآولا رورت مقدمه دن لابدر که
مقصود کتاب معلوم ما اولا آمدی اولعقد نا تکی بینکو نوع ایده لم المقدة الاولی فی العجب
عجبتواغیر درک السان نه عارضی اولور بر نسنه دن که کم معرفت قصوریکون یامو زک
اثرنده کیفیت تاثیری بلده وکی بچون آنک مثالی اگر بر کسه زنبورخانه نیس کور مشراولب
آنکو ریکبجرتکلو رآواچپ تدن که بلمازد که بو عجب شکالیم دوزمش در واگر آنک معلو
aolسه که بو نه زنبور امنش بر برجیرت ضخی حاصل اولور که بر حیوان صنعت پو مسند خانه لر
ضلع لری برنه مساوی بچه دوزمشر که مهندس اگر که کاملو لا آلات ایله آنه بو لید ایده مر [...]
translation: It is the case that a dull mind imagines and denies, but from a keen and discerning mind nothing that is known is denied, for Almighty God has infinite power to create things. Some of these things are among the wonders of the craft of the Almighty God, some of which are perceived by the senses and some known by rational proof, and they occasion wonder either because they are heard about or because of their strange properties, which are known through reports. For example, one person tells another of a death and yet if at present some reports turn out contrary to expectation, it is meaningless to abandon all matters on account of a contrary example in some of them. For sometimes the non-conformity occurs because a condition is not found, or because some impediment exists. Consider the example of the magnet and the ant: if the distances of the magnet's sphere are exceeded, the property of the magnet is nullified, and just as when vinegar is applied the property returns. If one were to place a magnet near an anthill, one must know that both magnet and ant hill need to be examined, and it is necessary to know that what is unknown and what is an obstacle, and for this purpose the introduction is indispensable so that the aim of the book becomes clear. Let us now begin — **the First Introduction: On the Wondrous**. Wonder arises in the soul of a person as an accidental state on account of something of which he has little knowledge, or whose cause is unknown to him. For example, if someone has never seen a beehive and is told that the bees build it — that this creature constructs a house all of whose walls are equal — a complete engineer with all his instruments could not [surpass it]...
page_note: text page: introduction on the nature of wonder (al-'ajab), from the Ottoman Turkish translation of Qazwini's Aja'ib al-makhluqat

text:
وتوموی قازنن تحصیل‌لمش‌در و آن‌نچه قسمت‌لمش‌در که برخانه برخانه مخالف دکل‌در
کو سایر قالبه دو کلمش‌در و اول عسل‌ی قازنن کنو مشترک لاول‌غانه زلرده قومش‌در و آنفیش
ذخیره‌یه اولق‌یچون صافلمش‌در زیرانه پلور کیچون قیش‌لاواصحراده غذابولنز لیس‌
قیدش‌ی‌چون ذخیره کرک‌در و اولوکه نچه لمش‌در که بوخانه‌لری برنچه برده ایله اوزنگک کرگرتامول
عسل‌ی قاپمیه واکاتو زایر شوب فاسدالمیه سیرآنه اغزی و زلمش‌ی و سنکی‌ی لمش‌در پو تنغه
عجب‌در و برنسنه که عالمه کو رسن بوله درلگن آدم ابتداءصبا وندن بوعجایب‌ی کوره کلمش‌در
تاعقلی تمام اولوب عاشل‌مرز مشغول ولور لذات [...] انیه‌یه طالوب و آتوقوله عجایبه
کورکه مانوسلوب آکر تجیبلر نظر نن ساقطا اولور نجیت‌ب‌یده مرجون برعجب جیوان باعادی
مخالف برفعل کورسه نعجب‌یدیروب سبحانالله لاالاالله دیرآتا جمیع عمرنه نچیه لسندر
مشاهده‌ایدر که عقول عقلا و نفوض ذکیا اندن مدهوش‌لولورآکر بومعنی سکامصور
اولسون دیرسک نظر قیل فلاکه که بوکک‌بی اجسام رفیعه‌یه بو قدر روسعت ولودکلو صلا
ایله‌حق تعالی‌نجه حفظ ایدر تغیر و فسادون عمر دنیا تمام اُنچیدرک کو آرمیان و مع افلاک
نسبت برحلقه‌که درصحراده دو تمش‌حق تعالی بوری‌به وَالسَّمَاء بَنَيْنَاهَا بِأَيْدٍ وَإِنَّا
لَمُوسِعُون اندن صکره نظر قل فونک دوران مختلفنه که بعض‌ینه نسبت رخوی‌در
و بعضه دولابه در و بعضه حامیلی در و بعضه حرکتی سریع و بعضنک بطلی
اندن صکره نظر قل دوام حرکتنه که هیچ بورلسی و طور لسمی بوقدر لسمی آن صکن
نظر قل‌که بنده بناغه در دیر کسنز و علاقه‌سز و آندن صکره نظر قل بلدز لرک کرک
translation: ...and the honey that has been gathered is unlike that found in other hives, for it has been brought together from common sources and stored in it as a reserve, purified so that it may be used in winter when food cannot be found in the fields or plains — for storage is necessary. And it has been arranged so that these chambers, filled with honey one by one, are sealed with wax so that the honey does not spoil or ferment or become contaminated. It is a wonder that a person who comes to see this spectacle of nature, from the first morning he observes these marvels, until his reason is fully mature and he is preoccupied with the pleasures [...] aspiring to its wonders — he sees them as familiar things and is no longer astonished; yet if an animal of a contrary nature performs an unusual act, he says 'How wondrous! Subhanallah! La ilaha illallah!' — yet he has spent his whole life without observing this. Such things astound the intellects of the learned and the minds of the wise. If you wish to picture this meaning, look at the celestial sphere: how these vast, refined bodies are preserved by Almighty God with such magnitude and fullness from alteration and corruption throughout the entire age of this world, and between the spheres in relation to a ring dropped in a desert, as the Most High says: 'And the heaven We constructed with strength, and indeed, We are [its] expander.' Then after that, look at their different rotations — some of which are slow, some like a waterwheel, some carrying [others], some swift in motion, and some slow. Then after that, look at the constancy of their motion: that not one of them ever rests or stops, so great [is their movement] without pause. Then look at how it is without foundation, without support, and without attachment. And after that, look at the stars...
page_note: text page: cosmological discussion of bees, celestial spheres, and divine creation, with Quranic citation (al-Dhariyat 51:47) in red

text:
وضعنه و شمس و قره و بو‌نلكر اختلاف مشارق و مغاربنده كه اختلاف اوقات
سببی ایله حیوانات و نباتات ناشی اولور آندن صكره نظر قل كو آلنكه بیر شه
وانك نازلنده كه حساب مقرر در میج تخلف اتمز و نقصان و زیاده اولز و نظر
قل كو آلنك عددنده و كثرتنده و لونلرك اختلافنده كه بعضنی قزلغنه مایل و بعضی
اقلعنه مایل و بعضی قلای رنكنده در آندن صكره نظر قل شمسك فلكده سیرنه
كه بر بلده دورن تمام ایدر و بر كون طلوع ایدر و غروب ایدر و كیجه‌نك و كونرك
حالنده كه وقت معاش و وقت راحت ایچون نظر و كیجه‌نك و كونزك اوزمسنه
و فصلمسنه كه شمسك وسط سادون میلی ایله اولور و بونك ایله فصول ربعه
حاصل اولور و آصاب علم میاة اتفاق المثل در جرم شمسك عظمنه كه أشد
و فلك اعظم جمله عالمی محیط ایكن آنك سرعت حركتنه و بو سوزك مصداته در بو
حكایت ـــــ رسول الله صلی الله علیه وسلم بر وقت ظهر قریب
اولدعی زمانده كه جبرائیل علیه السلام حاضر ایدی دیدی كه یا جبرائیل ظهر
نمازنك وقتی اولدیمی جبرائیل علیه السلام دیدی رسول الله افضل
الصلوات دیدی كه یا جبرائیل بو كلام ندر جبرائیل دیدی یا رسول الله سؤال
اتدك و قده در خو ظهرا و المشل ایدی بن آلادیجه دك شمس بر شبوز ملكی بو‌لیم
ایلدی و آندن صكره نظر قل جرم قره‌یه قبول اولور آیدر آنفابارن ناكجیده قایم مقام
افتاب اولور تعده كیجه‌دن كیچی یقصا قبول یدروب محاقه مبتلا اولور و آندن صكره نظر
translation:
...and the sun and the moon, and these [luminaries] differ in their risings and settings, which is the cause of the difference of times, whence arise animals and plants. Consider, then, how in their number there is no increase or decrease, and in the number of these [stars] and their multiplicity and the difference of their colors — some inclined toward redness, some toward paleness, and some of a silvery hue — after that, consider the course of the sun in its sphere: how it completes one full circuit of a town, rising in the day and setting, and the state of night and day — the time of livelihood and the time of rest — and the lengthening and shortening of night and day, which comes about through the sun's mean declination, and by this the four seasons come about. The scholars of hydrology agree that the magnitude of the solar body is the greatest, and the supreme sphere encompasses the entire world; [consider] how swift its motion is, and this saying is attested by the following:

HIKAYA (ANECDOTE): When the time of the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) for the midday [prayer] was approaching, and Gabriel (peace be upon him) was present, he [the Prophet] said: 'O Gabriel, has the time of the noon prayer come?' Gabriel (peace be upon him) said: 'O Messenger of God, [you are] the best of prayers [to ask].' The Prophet said: 'O Gabriel, what is this saying?' Gabriel replied: 'You asked, and indeed at noon I had gone [to inquire] — before I could descend, one of the angelic kings of the sun had already made [the reckoning]. Then consider how the disc [of the moon] receives [light], appearing as if a deputy of the sun has been appointed there; then again it passes through the night diminishing until it falls into conjunction (muhāq), and after that consider how...'
page_note: text page — discussion of the sun, moon, stars, their motions and seasons, followed by a hadith-anecdote about Gabriel and the noon prayer

text:
شمسك سوفنه و قرقز سوفنه و نظر قل قریبوز نده و الان قره لغده قابل نور دکلدر
و نظر قلا کاعر بلر مجبره و عملر راه کر کشان و روم الملاجاحیلر بولی وصأا و غریبی
و بو نلرک سببی بیان اولنسه کر مرو عجاب بمو اتحصر لو فرآندن صکره نظر قل عجایبه
آسمان و زمیان اورتسنده در شرها بکلیق و سحابحادثا اولوق و کوکک کورلکک و شمشک
بلورک و یلدرم اولوق و تقو ر باغوق و مختلف بلار اسک و نقیل بو لندر بیدا اولوق
هوای صافیده و آول بولندمستخر اولوق بیلده که مللا انلری سور حقو تغالی سور دنغم
وار رو آنده بغور باغدورز و تیمور قطره لری بربرنه او لاشمیوب قطره بره قطره به نمک
ویر کر آنی بوده بات بنک اگر بربرده متصل اولبو لوق دن دوکلو ر کی دوکلیدی
براری برترو اکنلری خراب ایدر ایدی و اکر جاحت مقدارندن اکسک اولیدی نباتات حاصل
اولمز ایدی قرآن مجیده بو کا اشارت و اردر کر خو بقا سوره وَالَّذِي أَنزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً بِقَدَ
اندن صکره نظر قل بلار کر اغذاف نه کیجه سند بولنگر سورر و بلار کر بعضی بلونگر طاٸی
و بعضی جمع ایدر و تعبئه اکنلری و کیشلری اسلری و بعضی قوریدر و نظر قل بلار کر
اختلافنه کیرده و نباته نیجه درلو نصرف ایدرار و نظر قل بره که نیجه فراش و مرها آوشم
و ند کلو دوشمشی نیجه واسع در شو کیر کآدمی دو کلی عمر نده کز سه انکلطا فذایره مر وحقو تغا
بویرر وَالْأَرْضَ فَرَشْنَاهَا فَنِعْمَ الْمَاهِدُوْنَ و بر کلوز رن مسکن آجهایا والیچی مقر آموت
ایگر آند نظر قل بره قوری طوبراقی لیکن اکا بغور ایر اکا بغو رایر رنا رتن و معدن نون و حیولنلن
عجایب حادثا اولو روحق تعالی سوره فَانظُرْ إِلَى آثَارِ رَحْمَتِ اللَّهِ كَيْفَ يُحْيِي الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا
translation: The sun's course and the Pleiades' course — observe those nearby; now in the dark [regions] there is no accessible light. And observe how the great ones are compelled, and the laborers, wayfarers, travelers, those of Rome and the surrounding lands; both the well-provided and the stranger. The reason for these [things] shall be explained: after the marvels are enumerated, one is directed to contemplate the wonders between heaven and earth — the accumulation of clouds in the sky, the thickening of clouds, rumbling of thunder and flashing of lightning, the appearance of crystal-like [hail] and thunderbolts, their manifestation in the pure air. It is known that all of these [atmospheric phenomena] are made subservient — [as the text says] that their drops come together, [the clouds] meeting one another, drop by drop, like salt [grains], each joining the other, flowing and pouring. Thus they water the surrounding lands. If [rain] fell short of the needed measure, vegetation would not come forth. The Holy Qur'an points to this in Surah al-Zukhruf [or similar]: 'And it is He who sends down water from the sky in due measure.' — After this, observe the clouds: how at night they spread out over the lands, how some are dry and some collect and store [water] like storehouses for winter supplies; and some [clouds] are parched. Observe the clouds in their variety, how they transform vegetation in numerous ways. And observe how the carpet [of earth] is spread — like a bed and a resting-place — how vast it is! A human being could not traverse it in a lifetime. As God Most High says: 'And the earth — We have spread it out; how excellent are We who spread it!' And it provides dwelling-place for souls, a place of abode for the living and the dead. And then observe the dry earth, yet within it God has deposited ores, minerals, and living creatures of wondrous kinds. And God Most High says: 'Look then at the traces of God's mercy — how He gives life to the earth after its death.'
page_note: text page, folio 147, Ottoman Turkish prose discussing wonders of sky, rain, clouds, and earth, with embedded Qur'anic citations in red

text:
آندن صکره نظر قل بر که جوانبنده کآغرطاغلر جانب صیحکیده منع ادرک گذن و آندن
صکره آیه صو خرزینه سی قبلدی که صولر و مغوره لر مغاره لرده و کو بلدرده ابر کیلور و آزآن
اندرن چقر و آنلردن اشبلار و ارمقلد ظاهر ا ولو رکه سبب نبات و حیوان اولو رتا کالچک
قدیمه دکگه صواره مرد اولا و توصو رکک رایه قلآ دکزاره دوکلور آن صکره نظر قل
دکزار وطاغلر و معور بر کرکره آیه بنسبت بر کو چیکک جزیره کبی بر سوک جر اچیجنده و یتچی رصو
التندن قالمش در آن صکره نظر قل کزارک عجابنده که عجیب شکل حیوانلر وارد و جمو وجموان که
قروده واردرانکه مثلیک گزده واردر وصو ده حیوانات اولو رکه قرو ده آنانکه مثل او لاز آندر صکره
نظر قال گرک جو بر نه ودرک گزده صد قالیجنده انجو حادثا ولدر وغنو نظر قاص والچینده بر کطاشن
اغاج بتکی مرجان تند وکنه و تنظر قال قیمتلو طا شلر و عنبر و نفایس اعیان که دکر انکر کنارارمز
و نظر قال اغز تو که کو میاره و انلکر سر عت سیر نبیل قو قه ایلده و دکگک عجابه بجهد رجمع و بیّا
او لنفعه قابل دکلر آن صکره نظر قال انواع معادنکه بعضی بومشبوب ترکیب و یتجی قلمنعه
قابل درالتون و کومشر و بقر وقلای و دیمور کسی وتعضو بومشبوب ترکیب لونفعه قابل
دکلد ریاقوت و زبرجد و بیروزکی و نظر قل بر که معدنلر کبعضنه کنفط و کرتو قطر آن
حادثا ولور وجملهٔ معدنلر کل دناسی طوز در اکر بر شهر خلقطور بولمیو بطوز نر طعام
یسه آنکا بلده فساد ابر را ادرر آن صکره و نظر قل می وه کرکاصنه فنا شکاگر ولوندری
والنکر و رالچیکر بر نه مخالفنه بآوجو دکه بر صو دن حاصل اولو رکه حق تعالی بوری [نشانی؟]
و نفضل بعضها علی بعض فی الأكل وبردانه دن نیچه دانه حاصل اولورکه حق تعالی بیور
translation: Then look how on the sides there are high mountains which prevent [winds] from passing, and after that the water-treasures descend toward the qibla, so that the waters flow into the caves and valleys, and from there they emerge and from them rivers and streams appear on the surface, which are the cause of plants and animals coming into being until ancient times. Look then at how the seas spread out, poured into vast expanses, and after that look at what lies between the seas and mountains: like a small island in the midst of the water, enclosed, left remaining underneath. From there, look at the wonders: strange-shaped animals are there, and creatures such as have no equal exist there, and in the water live animals, and on dry land those that have no equal. Then look at how in the depths of the sea, in the pearl-diving places, accidents occur and pearls are formed, and look at how on its shores there are precious timbers of coral, and valuable stones and ambergris and rarities, such that other shores have none. Look at how the ships sail with great speed upon it, and gather from it all benefits, bringing them together, so that they become useful. Not all of these are [yet] comprehended. Look how in those islands there are all kinds of minerals—some of which are well-composed in their constitution and thus useful—such as gold, silver, copper, tin, and iron; and some, though well-composed, are not useful in their constitution. And look at how rubies, emeralds, and turquoise [are found], and look at how among the minerals some produce naphtha and tar and [other substances]. The sum of all minerals is salt: if the people of a city found no salt and ate food without salt, it would bring corruption to that land. Look then at how fruits differ from one another: though they come from the same water, each is different and of a different character, as God Most High has said [in the Quran]: 'We have made some of them excel others as food.' And from a single grain, many grains are produced, as God Most High says...
page_note: text page, cosmographical prose on minerals, seas, islands, and plants from Qazwini's Aja'ib al-makhluqat

text:
كَمَثَلِ حَبَّةٍ أَنْبَتَتْ سَبْعَ سَنَابِلَ فِي كُلِّ سُنْبُلَةٍ مِائَةُ حَبَّةٍ اندن صكره نظر قلوقى
يره كه مغور لوبخو حركت ايدر و بويور و بيتور ر مجنس نانه نيتكه كم حق تعاله بويور
فَإِذَا أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَيْهَا الْمَاءَ اهْتَزَّتْ وَرَبَتْ وَأَنْبَتَتْ مِنْ كُلِّ زَوْجٍ بَهِيجٍ اندن صكره
نباتاتكه جو قابلغی ايله واروا قنك واشكالنك وطعامنك و رايحه لرنكه كمال فايلكجيب
حاصر كروغريبه منفعتكر واردر بيجه براوت بو قدركه آنده برمنفعت بلكه برنيجه منفعت
كه بعضه آدم بلور و بعضه اينجو خوتعاله بيلور آنندن صكره نظر قالحيوانانكه الوانعه
بعضه مواده اوجر و بعضه يوزر و بعضه براوزر نده بورر كيمى كى باغ اوزركيمى
دورت یاغ اوزركيمى برنيجه ياغ اوزركيمى قرنه اوزره آندن صكره نظر قالحيو لنكرك
شكالنك وخوازنكر وفعاللرنكه كمال فذكه كجائب واردر آشول حده كه عقول عقلا
انده نجه آولور لر بلكه سورى سنكده وفرنجه ده وآريده واورمجكده كرلونه جيوانلكه جمله
اضعف بر لوناكه عجائب افعال انده فكر قالنج بخيه خانبنا ايدر لر وغذا ابى نيجه جمع ايدر لر
وآنيجه ذخيره ايدرلر واورمجكه نيجه آغه ايدركه تاكاصيد دوشر وبيجه برضعيف حيوان
بو قدركآنيزه جو قلوعجايله بله يه وحق تعالى بويور رقَالَ انْظُرُوا إِذَا فِي السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ
بسوخ نعاجه فرنكه خلقا تدوكى اشيانكه عجابنده ديدى بو قدر وتو برجر در كنارى كورنز
الْمُقَدِّمَةُ الثَّانِيَةُ فِي تَفْصِيلِ الْمَخْلُوقَاتِ مخلوق كه جو تعاله حق تركه غيرنه ديرلر شوندن خالى كلدر كه
ياقايم بذاته اولايا اوليه قايم بذاته اولان ذخيا منيجه اولا ماا وليكر منيجه اولور كه كاجيم
وكر نيجه اولنيكه كابو مروحاندر لاكر جو مروحاجه سمتعلق اوكور سته علق نده بيرلده اكا
translation:
— like a grain that grows seven ears, in each ear a hundred grains. After that, look at the earth: how it stirs and moves and grows and produces various kinds, just as God Most High says: 'When We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells and puts forth every delightful kind [of growth].' After that, consider how many wonderful forms, shapes, tastes, and fragrances are gathered in plants — benefits beyond counting, each one holding not just one benefit but many, some known to man, others known only to God Most High. After that, consider the animals and their various kinds: some move upon the ground, some swim, some run on four feet, some move in yet other ways — consider then the forms, features, and actions of animals, so wondrous that the minds of scholars are confounded by them. In each tiny living creature such marvels of action are found that scholars stand in bewilderment; they gather food in extraordinary ways and store provisions, and spiders weave their webs so that prey may fall into them — yet such a weak creature shows such wondrous ingenuity. God Most High says: 'Look at what is in the heavens and the earth.' He said: consider the marvels of all these things that God has created — this much and more you shall see at its margin.

The Second Introduction: On the Detailed Account of Created Beings. Whatever God Most High has created, other than Him, is called 'creation.' It is free from being either self-subsistent in its essence or subsisting in another that is self-subsistent in essence — for it must be one or the other; and if it is of the kind that subsists in another, like soul [rūḥ], then it relates to something else and is connected to it.
page_note: text page with Qur'anic quotations in red; begins mid-passage on wonders of plants and animals, then opens the Second Introduction on the classification of created beings
